accepted.evidence: DEDR827 explicitly lists Parji edram, edrom chest, beside Konda eduṟam chest and Kannada ede/erde chest, breast. The form is exact; the survey’s broad breast gloss is compatible with chest/bosom, but mammary-gland specificity is not independently established and remains a review qualification.
accepted.comparison: direct Parji attestation, qualifications stated in evidence

accepted.evidence: DEDR5516 explicitly gives Parji ven- (vett-, vend-) to hear, matching the survey ven- stem and meaning. Compare Ollari ven-, Telugu vinu and Kolami vin-; no derivational or borrowing step is asserted.
accepted.comparison: direct Parji attestation, qualifications stated in evidence

accepted.evidence: DEDR4344(a) explicitly gives Parji pun- (pund-, putt-) to know, exactly matching the source pun-. This is the knowing family, not the homonymous pun new in DEDR4275; the whole 4344 article is the parent.
accepted.comparison: direct Parji attestation, qualifications stated in evidence

accepted.evidence: DEDR4652 explicitly gives Parji maḍ- (maṭṭ-) to lie down, sleep, matching source maḍ- lie. Kolami maṛi-/maḍiy- has the same meaning. The borrowing qualification in the article concerns Brahui maṭṭa, not this Parji stem.
accepted.comparison: direct Parji attestation, qualifications stated in evidence

accepted.evidence: DEDR3120 gives Parji taṛuŋg liver beside Ollari taṛiŋ and Kolami tarŋguḍ. The survey taruṅg (house taruŋg) has plain r where DEDR writes ṛ; the otherwise close segmental and exact semantic match supports this family, with the rhotic transcription difference retained explicitly rather than silently corrected.
accepted.comparison: direct Parji attestation, qualifications stated in evidence

accepted.evidence: DEDR5381 explicitly gives Parji vāni (stem vān-) rain, exactly matching this source. Telugu vāna and Kolami vāna share the rain sense; the article includes both sky and rain, so its displayed head need not match the Parji sense.
accepted.comparison: direct Parji attestation, qualifications stated in evidence

accepted.evidence: DEDR868 explicitly gives Parji en- (end-, ett-) to say (so-and-so), matching source en- say. Kolami and Naiki en- provide nearby comparanda; the source’s citation-form hyphen is retained in Original and is not derivational morphology.
accepted.comparison: direct Parji attestation, qualifications stated in evidence
